task.description: FINAL re-check -- this is the last budgeted rework attempt (rework_count is already 2 of max_rework 3). Read lib/letflow/design/iss0911-start-instance-dialog-exact-lookup.md directly: the one-shot guard fix (step 3 reads-then-immediately-clears lookupWroteDefinitionId every run) plus the dialog-open/close reset. Independently verify the one-shot claim's own reasoning about the effect's dependency array (does the argument that 'exactly one run can ever observe a self-written definitionId before activeDefinitionByName resolves or versionLookupState routes elsewhere' actually hold, or is there a sequence where two runs both see the same self-written definitionId while activeDefinitionByName is still resolving, e.g. an unrelated re-render firing the effect a second time with the same dependencies before the query settles?). Also verify the dialog-open/close reset doesn't itself introduce a new gap (what if the guard fires between a close and the ref-clear, or vice versa). Run the complete Step 2 design gate over the whole document one more time. If this FAILs, state explicitly that this exhausts the run's rework budget so ORCH escalates rather than dispatching a fourth rework.
acceptance_criteria: the fix calls definitionsApi.getActive(name) (or an equivalent exact-match backend lookup) keyed on the dialog's own typed value, not the page-level filtered list
a race-guard against out-of-order async responses (rapid typing) is explicitly designed, not left implicit
the version field's loading/not-found/found states are all specified

a single write path for startDefinitionVersion/startDefinitionId is designed, with no possibility of the new effect's own setSearchParams call re-triggering a second, independent effect that transiently desyncs the two values

the guard/token distinguishing a self-caused definitionId change from an external one is one-shot/expiring, cannot be revived by an unrelated later event reaching the same id value, and is reset on dialog open/close

gate_history.summary: Two independent effects both wrote startDefinitionVersion/startDefinitionId; the new effect's setSearchParams call re-triggered the old effect before its cache had the new id.
issues: Design's own claim that the old effect was 'already-correct, untouched' didn't account for the new effect's setSearchParams reactivating it
gate_history.next_action: Fold both effects into a single write path.

gate_history.summary: lookupWroteDefinitionId was a persistent, non-expiring guard token -- an unrelated later external definitionId change coincidentally matching a previously-self-written value fooled the guard into skipping an update, leaving fields stuck at stale data.
issues: Guard never cleared/consumed, never reset on dialog open/close
gate_history.next_action: Make the guard one-shot/expiring or generation-token based, reset on dialog open/close.
